reviews.title: Getting Better
reviews.text:
I have been health and fitness focused for 54 years. Upon reading the first ad for Hume, I was intrigued. I purchased the original band. At the time, the hardware, the firmware, the software, had some challenges. They worked diligently with me to improve.

Upon receipt of my 2.0 band, some things were strikingly better. There is still visible room for improvement. Biological ages on different screens do not match. The rate of walking or running per mile is still not even close. Heart rate while exercising is inconsistent, but improving. The most glaring essential improvement is to get the band either with its own GPS or linking to an Apple GPS. I look forward to the next three months of improvements. 

Though not perfect, I have found no plan or device superior. I intend to consistently feedback to Hume until the system is correct.

For anyone new to Hume, it’s not perfect and it’s an ever evolving ecosystem. Overall it’s been a positive experience and I hope the development team continues to improve and grow the product. reviews.title: Longtime User. Good concept but needs improvement.
reviews.text:
I’ve used the Hume Pod consistently for over a year and a half, so my review is based on long-term experience rather than just a few weigh-ins. There are things I really like about the scale. I appreciate the amount of information it provides, and the app presents body-composition data in an easy-to-understand way. However, for the price of the scale plus the yearly subscription, I expected a more consistent experience.

My biggest concern is the amount of day-to-day fluctuation in the body-composition measurements. I understand that hydration, exercise, food intake and other factors can affect BIA readings, but when a product is marketed with very high accuracy claims and comparisons to DEXA, I think consumers naturally expect a high level of consistency from the measurements.

Travel has also been frustrating. There is currently no vacation or travel mode, and I have experienced disruptions in my data after being away. When I contacted customer service about this, they initially assumed I also owned a Hume Band and explained that the band could continue collecting data while I was traveling, although those measurements would not be as accurate as actually stepping on the Hume Pod. I do not own the band, which would be an additional purchase on top of the scale and subscription.

I was eventually advised that after returning from a trip, I may need to step on the Pod several times for it to regulate again. That doesn’t really solve the issue I was asking about. I would much rather see Hume add a vacation/travel mode that recognizes a planned break in measurements and allows users to resume normally when they return.

Customer service has been another disappointment. My response regarding the travel issue took long enough that I could potentially have already been away on my trip before receiving the information. In a previous communication, Hume even acknowledged that their customer service needed improvement, but unfortunately my own experience has not shown much improvement yet.

I like the concept of the Hume Pod and think it has a lot of potential, which is why I’ve continued using it for more than 18 months. But at this price point, especially with an ongoing yearly fee, I think customers should receive more consistent performance, better travel functionality and more responsive customer support.

For now, I feel three stars fairly reflects my experience. I would be happy to update my review if these areas improve.

reviews.title: They take away features over time
reviews.text:
Very disappointing. You buy the hardware, then they take the useful data away.
I bought the Hume Health band because the pitch was simple: pay once for the equipment and see your own health data, including sleep detail, without a monthly fee. That is not how it works in practice.
After I was told to update the app, the detailed sleep breakdown I had been using was gone. Stages, timing, and the night-by-night detail that made the band worth wearing overnight were locked behind a paywall. The hardware did not change. The sensors did not change. An update changed what I was allowed to see from a device I already paid for.
Sleep tracking was the main reason I bought it. A score with the useful detail stripped out is not the same product. Pushing an update that moves core data behind a subscription feels like a bait and switch. If detailed sleep was always going to be a paid feature, that should have been clear before purchase, not after the update prompt.
The band itself is comfortable enough to sleep in, and the idea of a screenless tracker is fine. The business model is the problem. I already bought the equipment. I should not have to subscribe to keep seeing the sleep data that device collected.
Would not recommend unless you are willing to pay monthly for features that used to be included.
Shorter version if a review box has a character limit:
Bought the band, was told to update, then lost the detailed sleep data behind a paywall. The hardware did not change. An app update did. Sleep detail was the reason I bought it. Paying once for the device and then being charged again to see your own sleep stages is very disappointing. Do not buy if you expect the data you paid for to stay available.

reviews.title: Accuracy?
reviews.text:
The HUME BODY SCALE requires no set- up other than downloading the app onto your phone. From there you can access directions etc., and how to use the scale. 

It doesn’t have to be recalibrated—in fact there is no option to do so — unlike  another scale I have that doesn’t similar measurements including muscle:fat percentages and ratios. That makes me wonder about the accuracy of HUME, perhaps the scale automatically recalibrates itself each time so the user doesn’t have to ( I move it around so it’s never in one location, which is why I have to recalibrate the other scale). 

It takes about 20-seconds or so to get weight and internal measurements before it completes the weigh-in. If you try and weigh yourself again immediately after a warning message pops up saying that it’s too early for your next weigh in (therefore it won’t accept it)  and to wait 24- hours. But you can override this message by deleting the previous weigh in first. 

I don’t subscribe to the in-depth analysis and the scale still provides you with fat versus muscles in lbs/kg or in percentages. It also gives you an internal age, based on these factors and compared to health data  from medical standards and other people in your gender, age, and height class.

It’s best to use this and any other like scale as a way to compliment your yearly health checkups with a doctor because there are plenty of issues that this scale cannot detect, so it’s limited as far as being the only thing you need as an indicator of your overall health.

I can (& do) do the math when I create a recipe, using the specific ingredients and weights I use, because accuracy is important.  I find the Ai generated counts to be wildly off, sometimes up to 50%.  That isn’t a slam on the technology because it’s hard to tell from a photo what goes into a recipe…even though I manipulate serving sizes to make the calorie count correct I know the macros are wrong so that makes the advice it gives for your nutrition incorrect because for a computer bad data = bad results. reviews.title: Over priced - under delivered
reviews.text:
For the cost of the premium subscription, this should work as well as Apple fitness and MyFitnessPal pal. It’s lacking many options that lower cost apps offer. My suggestions to make it worth the cost would be to fix the following deficiencies:
Nutrition tab: - 
[ ] Lacks many barcodes
[ ] Can’t add recipes (screenshots)
[ ] Doesn’t show macro goals
[ ] Doesn’t show full nutrition (fiber, fat breakdown, vitamins, etc)
[ ] Needs a timer for intermittent fasting 
[ ] Allow preplanning of meals with times in the future. 
[ ] Allow adding multiple items from the recent meals search

Activity tab:
[ ] Should show heart zone minute goals (including accumulated zones 4 & 5) in activity mode or allow switching between activity tab and home tab. 
[ ] More options needed for activity mode (boxing, dancing, etc)

reviews.text:
I have both the Humeband 2.0 and the Homepod 1.0. I've been using it since September 1st. Every night my sleep has been tracked, yet on my health reports there's no sleep. It says there's been no data collected, which is crazy.

The same thing was happening with my body composition as well. I was getting data every day on one part of the app, but nothing was being propagated into the the weekly health report, until recently.

I reached out to customer service several times, with an initial response asking for screenshots and information on the model of iPhone I was using, which iOS version, etc. And radio silence after that. Reached out several more times, more radio silence.

Not sure why my data, which is showing as being collected in one part of the app, is not propagating into the reports. And no one's been able to give me an answer or even respond. This has influenced my decision to not subscribe to this app and just use the free version.

Still, it is useful to see the trends and the price (with discount) seems reasonable.

The visceral fat index is useless because there is no description of how the metric is calculated, what it means, or what the top and bottom numbers are. There has to be a more useful way to present the information.

reviews.title: Received What Appears to Be a Used Product — 4 Weeks of Silence From Customer Service
reviews.text:
I ordered a Hume Band on September 2, expecting to receive a brand-new product. Instead, the device arrived without its protective covering and had visible scratches on the sensor area, leaving me questioning whether I had been sent a previously used or returned device.

I contacted Hume immediately after receiving it to report the problem.

On September 10, their customer service team acknowledged my complaint and indicated that they would provide a brand-new replacement once the issue was verified. They requested photographs of the device, which I promptly submitted that same day.

That was the last meaningful communication I received.

Despite sending multiple follow-up emails, I have received no replacement, no shipping confirmation, and no meaningful explanation. One of their responses was a generic message that appeared to completely disregard our previous correspondence, as though I were contacting them for the first time.

Ironically, Hume had specifically informed me that they were consolidating my support tickets to streamline communication and resolve the issue more efficiently. Instead, I’ve experienced weeks of delays and an almost complete lack of communication.

What’s particularly concerning is their 45-day return policy. As the days continue to pass without resolution, I’m increasingly concerned that their lack of response could leave me outside the return window before they address my complaint.

I have no way of knowing whether these delays are intentional, but the experience has seriously undermined my confidence in this company.

I paid for a brand-new product, received one that appeared used or damaged, immediately reported the issue, and provided every piece of documentation requested. I should not have to repeatedly chase a company simply to receive the product I originally purchased.

At this point, I’m still waiting for Hume to honor its replacement commitment or provide a full refund.

My advice to prospective buyers: Pay close attention to the return policy and customer service experience before purchasing. A company’s willingness to stand behind its products matters just as much as the products themselves.

This has been an extremely disappointing experience.
